subject.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers

question: Should OpenClaw make this DeepSeek repair a public `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache` contract with an automatic DeepSeek default and explicit false rollback, or reject the new config surface in favor of a generic config-free message-shaping policy?
rationale: Both approaches can repair the observed regression, but they create different permanent user configuration, upgrade, and cross-provider contracts; repository policy requires provider/config ownership intent rather than an automated choice.

options.title: Approve the narrow DeepSeek contract
options.body: Accept the new compat field, DeepSeek-only automatic default, same-authority trailing carrier, and explicit false rollback, then require refreshed green exact-head checks before merge.

options.title: Use an internal config-free policy
options.body: Avoid a public knob and select or revise the generic sibling approach only after proving its broader OpenAI-compatible provider scope and upgrade safety.

options.title: Keep the behavior opt-in only
options.body: Retain the compat field but remove the automatic DeepSeek default, avoiding an upgrade-time payload change at the cost of leaving affected users to configure the repair manually.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow DeepSeek contract
recommendation.body: Accept the new compat field, DeepSeek-only automatic default, same-authority trailing carrier, and explicit false rollback, then require refreshed green exact-head checks before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is the merged commit that established the provider prompt-cache boundary behavior this PR modifies.
